:::{#rem-tarski-identities}
#### Tarski's high school identities

Restricted to positive integers,
the following results are
[Tarski's eleven "high school" identities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarski%27s_high_school_algebra_problem):

- sums are symmetric and associative (@thm-sum-symmetric, @thm-sum-assoc);
- multiplying by 1 changes nothing (@thm-mult-one);
- products are symmetric and associative (@thm-prod-symmetric, @thm-prod-assoc);
- multiplication is distributive (@thm-mult-distr);
- $1^b = 1$ and $a^1 = a$ (@thm-power-one);
- the power of a sum, of a product, and of a power
  (@thm-power-sum, @thm-power-product, @thm-double-exp).

Tarski asked whether every identity in $+$, $\times$, exponentiation and 1
that is true for all positive integers
can be derived from these eleven.
It cannot:
Wilkie found an identity that is true for all positive integers
but does not follow from them.
So this list is a useful core, not a complete rulebook.

:::
